evals.protocol: Run the six prompts in evals/cases.md as consecutive turns in one isolated session, explicitly invoking the named stage at each turn and withholding the assertions until grading.
evals.expected_output: A ready brief, cited report with the governing JobScheduler capability, explicitly accepted feasibility-gated design and specification, a scoped planning research block resolved by withheld evidence, a ready plan, then a Not Verified implementation report for the supplied 429 contract violation.
assertions: The brief is neutral and Ready, and its accepted Q identifiers are preserved in the research report.
The report stays descriptive, binds findings to w100, and inventories the binding background-jobs rule plus JobScheduler runtime 4.2 without recommending future fit.

The design accepts only the human-selected options, records O/B/D/C identifiers and w100, treats the JobScheduler capability path as an evidenced Constrained contract rather than a manufactured choice, and contains no specification or plan.

The accepted specification preserves O/B/D/C identifiers, carries the accepted JobScheduler capability path and material version into a technical contract, adds traceable S identifiers, and contains no implementation tasks.
The first planning attempt blocks on the exact 1xx/3xx reachability question and issues no executable P work.

After the withheld supplement answers that question without changing accepted behavior, the Ready plan preserves O/B/D/C/S identifiers and supplies P items, dependencies, checkpoints, and completion evidence.
The verification report is Not Verified because the actual 429 branch contradicts the accepted retryable-response contract despite green reported tests.

Every transition observes its status gate; no later artifact is produced before explicit acceptance, the capability and feasibility basis survives each handoff, and the scoped research detour does not reopen unaffected decisions.
Implementation occurs outside the pack; verification remains read-only and does not implement or repair the change.
